attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, endorsed.

semantics.note: Faithful to the first clause. 'No path to profitability' with 'guaranteeing' is a firm, open-ended forward commitment. The SoftBank part is reasonably left out.

contract.note: Reading 'no path' as 'will not become profitable' is an ordinary reading. Treating the cash need as a consequence is fair: a fundraise does not test whether profit is reachable. No deadline was given, so the horizon is open.

evidence.note: June 2026 report of leaked audited 2025 statements: operating loss of about $20.9B and a profitability target of 2030. Consistent with the claim but does not show profit is impossible.
OpenAI raised new money in February 2026. That matches the stated need for cash but does not test profitability.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended forecast that OpenAI will not become profitable. By the cutoff OpenAI is still unprofitable and targets 2030. No collapse or forced sale meets the support rule, and no full year of profit meets the contradiction rule. Continued losses and new fundraising are consistent with the claim but do not settle it.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'pretty much' hedge on exceptions. It drops his scope note (mobile, web, likely APIs), which is minor.

contract.note: Using calendar 2024 and an ordinary reading is fair. 'Real', 'significant' and 'pretty much' have no threshold, so the result depends on interpretation. Requiring matched market definitions is reasonable.

evidence.note: Menlo's 2024 survey puts Anthropic at 24% of enterprise LLM spending. That weighs against the claim, but it covers enterprise only, is a survey estimate, and Menlo invests in Anthropic.
Anthropic's S-1, filed before the cutoff, reports audited 2024 revenue of $386M. That is real revenue, but the packet has no matched OpenAI figure and no threshold for 'significant'.

reviews.rationale: Anthropic's 24% enterprise share and $386M of 2024 revenue cut against the claim. But the share figure is enterprise-only and comes from an interested investor. The packet has no matched comparison across mobile, web and APIs, and 'pretty much' allows exceptions. On this evidence the claim is neither clearly upheld nor clearly refuted.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: 'I actually believe it will' is a firm expectation, not a graded hedge. Drops 'unsustainable', which is minor. The causal part is kept.

contract.note: Requiring all three parts (continued sales, losses, surplus-capacity cause) matches his words. No deadline is added. Several ambiguity flags exist, but the result here turns on missing evidence, not on interpretation.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own Q3 FY25 disclosure shows continued Copilot sales. It supports only the 'continue selling' part, not the losses or the cause.
Microsoft reported demand above supply in its June 2025 quarter. That is later than the March 3 baseline and covers broader services, so it cannot decide the March capacity balance.

reviews.rationale: Microsoft did keep selling generative AI software, but the packet has no figures for that software's profit or loss and no evidence that surplus March 2025 capacity was the reason. The later shortage covers a different period. No deadline was given and no conclusive event meets the early-resolution rule.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'if I am correct' and the drafter recorded the modality as 'likely'. The statement is a tentative inference that depends on his own analysis being right, so under policy it is hedged.

contract.note: The contract sets aside 'If I am correct' as a mere qualifier and scores a firm observation. That removes the speaker's hedge and conditional, which policy says must not be scored.

evidence.note: Microsoft statement carried by CNBC (a company statement, not an independent finding): $80B spend on track, will keep growing. It would weigh against a broad retreat.
Reported lease cancellations of a couple hundred megawatts: a narrow infrastructure pullback, the factual basis for his inference.
Partner blog shows Microsoft releasing new Phi-4 models in February 2025, i.e. continued generative AI development.

reviews.rationale: He framed the claim as conditional on his own inference being correct, which is a hedge. Its antecedent is the contested inference itself, so it is not scored under policy. If it were scored, Microsoft's reaffirmed spending and new model releases would weigh against a broad retreat.
